The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the narrative's thematic goals. Because the plot centers on the slow, grinding attrition of institutional bureaucracy and ongoing construction, the author relies heavily on **compression of time**, summarizing an entire academic year (from October to the end of term in spring) in just a few pages. Weeks of drilling, logging noise in spreadsheets, and enduring chemical smells are condensed into brisk, witty paragraphs that effectively convey the prolonged, repetitive misery of the faculty without boring the reader.

At the same time, the author uses **stretching of time** (or slowing down to real-time scenes) at exactly the right moments to ground the story emotionally and comedically. For example, the opening paragraph stretches out the few seconds it takes for the first drop of water to gather and fall, mirroring the protagonist's quiet observation. Later, time slows down for brief, punchy exchanges of dialogue—such as the meeting with the "Senior Stakeholder Liaison"—and in the final scene, where the quiet, real-time moment of Marguerite adjusting the bucket in her empty office allows her internal shift from frustration to "grim tenderness" and resignation to fully resonate.
